neighbours.label: ' as' right after an appearance verb (seem, feel, look, sound), opening 'as if'/'as though'; not comparative or role 'as'
fire: When the lights went out it felt as though the whole house was holding its breath.
From the road it looked as if nobody had lived there for years.
On the phone she sounded as though she had been crying.
By the third week it seemed as if the rain would never stop.
After the race my legs felt as if they belonged to someone else.
To the neighbours it appeared as though the shop had closed for good.
With the music playing it almost seems as though no time has passed.
At the end of the speech he looked as though he might faint.
quiet: When the lights went out the house was as quiet as a church.
From the road it looked like nobody had lived there for years.
On the phone she worked as an interpreter for the hospital.
By the third week the rain was twice as heavy as before.
After the race my legs were as stiff as boards.
To the neighbours he was known as the man who closed the shop.
With the music playing, time passes just as quickly as ever.
At the end of the speech he served as host for the dinner.

notes: Card: ' as' x6 ('feeling as though', 'seems as if'), also ' (' after if/elif in code, 'inside of', 'either,'. Probes: feeling as though 0.69, seems as if 0.68, inside of 0.44, 'either,' 0.70; 'as tall as' 0.01, 'acted as a guide' 0.01, 'looks like' 0.01, 'if (' only 0.09. The other card contexts (a linking word right after a head that takes a clause) are not covered by this label, so it is likely partial.
